speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing your symptoms. To help narrow this down, have you noticed any sudden onset of these symptoms, or did they develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned an increased intake of garlic recently; did you consume raw garlic or large quantities of supplements alongside it? Additionally, have you noticed any sensitivity to light or sound, or any changes in your vision besides the dizziness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) secondary to recent viral illness. The history of a "sustained" spinning sensation with relief from diphenhydramine is more consistent with vestibular neuritis or labyrinthitis than BPPV (which is typically episodic and position-triggered), but MS is highly unlikely given the age and lack of other neurologic deficits. I recommend a Head Impulse Maneuver and Audiometry to confirm the diagnosis and rule out inner ear pathology.
